summary:
We have developed MONOCHROME - Planet X / SPHEREx, an open-source web application and asynchronous scientific computing pipeline for searching for analogs of Planet X and cold substellar objects with high proper motion, based on data from NASA’s SPHEREx infrared spectral survey and archival missions.

The platform integrates multi-year observation epochs through direct queries to the NASA/IPAC IRSA and CADC NEOSSat archives. Users can explore key calibration targets or any ICRS coordinates in four modes: the three-dimensional celestial sphere Orbital Vault, an epoch comparator with an interactive slider and a “Blink” mode, the SPHEREx spectral laboratory with 102 channels (0.75–5.0 μm) featuring blackbody models and absorption bands of molecules (CH₄, H₂O, CO, CO₂), as well as Live Explorer for setting up asynchronous tasks for cropping, adding, subtracting, and generating animations in FITS, PNG, and GIF formats.

MONOCHROME provides access to cutting-edge big data astrophysics, enabling citizen scientists and researchers to detect the smallest redshifts and cold brown dwarfs while maintaining full scientific rigor.
details:
What it does and how it works: 4 observation modes (3D orbital arc, epoch comparator with Split/Blink/Vector modes, 102-channel spectroscopy via segmented reading of FITS byte ranges, live search, and an asynchronous image processing worker on a common ICRS/TAN grid) + interactive training.

Advantages: Processing of gigabyte-sized FITS cubes on the server without the need for users to download them, uncompromising scientific accuracy (proper handling of archive errors, FLAGS quality masks, and dispersion), and synthesis of optical (NEOSSat) and infrared (SPHEREx) data.

Impact: Democratizing astronomy and accelerating the analysis of NASA’s open data through user-friendly visual tools.

Technology stack: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, Python 3.12+, FastAPI, Astropy, NumPy, SciPy, Reproject, SQLite, Docker, IRSA API, CADC TAP.

Factors taken into account: The specific characteristics of the 6 SPHEREx detectors (wavelength dependence on position), resilience to network delays in archives (caching, queues, worker), a bilingual interface (EN/RU), and support for keyboard navigation.
